newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Australian bonds wait for rate news, data.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Australian bonds wait for rate news, data.

text.p: *Australian bonds firm in SYCOM as U.S. market recoups Monday's losses on shortovering ahead of FOMC.
*9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) first window of opportunity for rate cut announcement by Reserve Bank, although not expected today.
*May retail trade, building approvals data out today.

Australian bonds consolidated the gains of a solid Tuesday seesion in overnight SYCOM trading, and look set to remain firm at least in the first hour of trade ahead of a possible rate cut announcement this morning.

Bonds put on some moderate gains as U.S. Treasuries reversed Monday's losses, with the market covering short positions ahead of the outcome of the FOMC meeting on Wednesday. The market is not expecting the Fed Reserve to announce a hike in U.S. rates.
Locally, the RBA's first opportunity to ease rates after Tuesday's meeting comes at 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT), although the market is not expecting an announcement on Wednesday.
Instead, a move on Thursday after the outcome of the FOMC is known, or after wage and inflation data is released later this month, is seen as more likely by the market.

For this reason, traders said that while bonds will be firm ahead of the possible announcement, pullbacks should be limited if there is no rate cut. Attention will then turn to May retail trade and building approvals data later in the morning.

Both series are forecast to show rises of 2.0 percent, with retail trade expected to reverse April's 1.7 percent fall and building approvals expected to be in line with other evidence of a modest housing upswing. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
